# API: Digital Humans

Digital Humans (`app` in the API) start work on a schedule, on events, or when someone messages them. Use these operations to install and remove them, pause and resume them, change their configuration, read their run history and activity, and chat with them.

Paths are relative to your Halo base URL, and every request carries the access password. Set `$HALO_URL` and `$HALO_TOKEN` as in the [quickstart](/en/developers/quickstart); base URL, authentication and error conventions are in the [HTTP API overview](/en/developers/api/).

## List digital humans (and other installed apps) in a space {#get-api-apps}

`GET /api/apps` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Optional query parameters: `spaceId` (only that workspace) and `status`. Without `status`, uninstalled Digital Humans are left out. Without `spaceId`, the list covers every workspace, as the Halo app shows it.
- `userConfig` and the `env` and `headers` of an MCP app's `spec.mcp_server` can hold credentials in plain text, and this API returns them as stored. Treat the response like a secret.

**Query parameters**: `spaceId`, `status`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{id,specId,spaceId,spec,status,userConfig,userOverrides,permissions,installedAt,lastRunAt?,lastRunOutcome?,errorMessage?}]}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/apps" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Get one installed digital human (or other app) by id {#get-api-apps-appid}

`GET /api/apps/:appId` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- `userConfig` and the `env` and `headers` of an MCP app's `spec.mcp_server` can hold credentials in plain text, and this API returns them as stored. Treat the response like a secret.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |


```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Soft-delete (uninstall) a digital human; recoverable via reinstall {#delete-api-apps-appid}

`DELETE /api/apps/:appId` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Uninstalls the Digital Human but keeps its data, so [`POST /api/apps/:appId/reinstall`](#post-api-apps-appid-reinstall) brings it back. The `purge=true` query parameter is accepted but currently has no effect.
- To delete it for good, call [`DELETE /api/apps/:appId/permanent`](#delete-api-apps-appid-permanent) afterwards.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Query parameters**: `purge`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX DELETE "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Clear a digital human's chat history {#post-api-apps-appid-chat-clear}

`POST /api/apps/:appId/chat/clear` <Badge type="danger" text="Irreversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

::: danger Irreversible
This cannot be undone, and nothing goes to a trash folder. Make sure it is what the user wants before you call it.
:::

- spaceId is required even though the app is already scoped to one. Optional conversationId clears one specific session instead of the default one.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "spaceId": "<spaceId — the app's own spaceId from GET /api/apps>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/chat/clear" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spaceId":"<spaceId — the app'\''s own spaceId from GET /api/apps>"}'
```

## Read a digital human chat transcript {#get-api-apps-appid-chat-messages}

`GET /api/apps/:appId/chat/messages` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Reads the main thread by default. For another thread pass `?conversationId=`, the same key [`POST /api/apps/:appId/chat/send`](#post-api-apps-appid-chat-send) takes.
- An empty list means the thread has no history yet, or the id is wrong — the two look the same. List the threads with [`GET /api/im-sessions`](/en/developers/api/channels#get-api-im-sessions) rather than guessing.
- `thoughts` holds the raw tool calls and results behind each reply and is large.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Query parameters**: `conversationId`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{id,role:"user"|"assistant",content,timestamp,thoughts?,thoughtsSummary?,images?}]}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/chat/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Send a message to a digital human and let it reply {#post-api-apps-appid-chat-send}

`POST /api/apps/:appId/chat/send` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- `spaceId` is the Digital Human's own workspace: the `spaceId` of its entry in [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps).
- `conversationId` picks the thread. Leave it out for the main thread. For a new thread, use the `conversationId` that [`POST /api/apps/:appId/sessions/create`](#post-api-apps-appid-sessions-create) returns. To continue a thread the user started in Halo, build it from [`GET /api/im-sessions`](/en/developers/api/channels#get-api-im-sessions) as `app-chat:&lt;appId&gt;:&lt;channel&gt;:&lt;chatType&gt;:&lt;chatId&gt;`.
- Only threads on the `local` and `http` channels are accepted. A thread that belongs to an IM chat is refused, so this API never speaks into a real conversation with a person. A malformed id returns 400 with the expected form; `chatId` may contain only letters, digits, `_` and `-`.
- Returns before the Digital Human has read the message. Follow the reply over the WebSocket, or poll [`GET /api/apps/:appId/chat/status`](#get-api-apps-appid-chat-status) until `isGenerating` is false and then read [`GET /api/apps/:appId/chat/messages`](#get-api-apps-appid-chat-messages), passing the same `conversationId` to both.
- A message sent while the same thread is still answering doesn't start a second session: it joins the running turn after its current step, or is merged into the next one. Send one message at a time and wait for the reply, so each reply answers one message.
- Optional body fields: `thinkingEnabled`, `reasoningEffort` (`off` to `max`; overrides `thinkingEnabled`, but the Digital Human's own setting wins), `images`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "spaceId": "<spaceId>",
  "message": "What did you find today?"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{conversationId}}  // accepted, not answered
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/chat/send" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spaceId":"<spaceId>","message":"What did you find today?"}'
```

## Check whether a digital human chat is currently generating a reply {#get-api-apps-appid-chat-status}

`GET /api/apps/:appId/chat/status` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Checks the main thread by default; pass `?conversationId=` for another thread, the same key [`POST /api/apps/:appId/chat/send`](#post-api-apps-appid-chat-send) takes.
- Poll with a growing interval (2 s, then double) instead of a fixed wait.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Query parameters**: `conversationId`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{isGenerating:boolean,conversationId}}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/chat/status" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Clear the history of all of a digital human's chats at once {#post-api-apps-appid-chats-clear-all}

`POST /api/apps/:appId/chats/clear-all` <Badge type="danger" text="Irreversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

::: danger Irreversible
This cannot be undone, and nothing goes to a trash folder. Make sure it is what the user wants before you call it.
:::

- Each chat is cleared as /clear clears it and starts afresh with its next message; replies in progress stop. API sessions, team chats, memory and reminders are left alone. Nothing is posted into the chats.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{cleared:number,failed:number}}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/chats/clear-all" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Answer a digital human's pending question (it stopped to ask a human before continuing) {#post-api-apps-appid-escalation-entryid-respond}

`POST /api/apps/:appId/escalation/:entryId/respond` <Badge type="danger" text="Irreversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

::: danger Irreversible
This cannot be undone, and nothing goes to a trash folder. Make sure it is what the user wants before you call it.
:::

- Answers a question a Digital Human asked during a run (an activity entry of type `escalation`; the Digital Human's status is `waiting_user` while it waits). Send `choice`, `text`, or both, as the question asked for; for a question with several parts, send `answers`, one `{choice?, text?}` per part, in order.
- This is the human decision the run was waiting for. Send the user's actual answer: it cannot be withdrawn afterwards.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |
| `entryId` | Activity entry id, from [`GET /api/apps/:appId/activity`](#get-api-apps-appid-activity). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "choice": "approve",
  "text": "optional free-text explanation"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{…the answered activity entry}} | {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/escalation/<entryId>/respond" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
```

## Read a digital human's transcript in a bound IM chat {#get-api-apps-appid-im-chat-messages}

`GET /api/apps/:appId/im-chat/messages` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- All three query params are required, 400 otherwise. spaceId must be the app's own — a different but valid one is accepted and reads the wrong space. Optional ?chatType=group, defaults to direct.
- channel is the session's IM channel (wecom-bot, feishu-bot, dingtalk-bot, weixin-ilink-bot); chatId is taken as [`GET /api/im-sessions`](/en/developers/api/channels#get-api-im-sessions) gives it. Any other channel, chatType or a chatId with whitespace, ":", "/", "\" or ".." is a 400. Read "http" and "local" sessions with [`GET /api/apps/:appId/chat/messages`](#get-api-apps-appid-chat-messages)?conversationId=.
- This is real correspondence with a person on the other end — read it only when the task needs it.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Query parameters**: `channel` (required), `chatId` (required), `spaceId` (required), `chatType`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{id,role:"user"|"assistant",content,timestamp,thoughts?,thoughtsSummary?,images?}]}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/im-chat/messages?channel=wecom-bot&chatId=<chatId — from GET /api/im-sessions>&spaceId=<spaceId — the app's own spaceId from GET /api/apps>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Merge-patch per-installation overrides (notification level, model) {#patch-api-apps-appid-overrides}

`PATCH /api/apps/:appId/overrides` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- JSON Merge Patch: send only the fields to change; `null` clears one (for example `{"modelSourceId":null}` falls back to the global model).
- Fields: `notificationLevel`, `modelSourceId`, `modelId`, `spaceMemoryAccess` (true lets the Digital Human read its workspace's memory topics), `chatReasoningEffort` (`off` to `max`, for its chats, IM replies and runs), `memory` (`{enabled, autoConsolidate, cadence}`, always the whole object; `cadence` is `diligent`, `balanced` or `economical`) and `disabledTools` (MCP apps only: tool names to leave out, the whole list each time; `[]` or `null` turns them all back on).
- A `modelSourceId` for an account that no longer exists is accepted; the Digital Human then runs on the current global account until the override changes.
- The run schedule is not set here; use [`POST /api/apps/:appId/frequency`](#post-api-apps-appid-frequency).

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "notificationLevel": "important"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX PATCH "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"notificationLevel":"important"}'
```

## Read what a run actually did, step by step {#get-api-apps-appid-runs-runid-session}

`GET /api/apps/:appId/runs/:runId/session` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- The transcript behind the "View process" panel — same shape as chat/messages, but for one automation run. It is the only way to see why a run did what it did rather than what it reported.
- Get the runId from [`GET /api/apps/<appId>/activity`](#get-api-apps-appid-activity). Read this when a run went wrong; for what it concluded, its activity entry is shorter and enough.
- Only a person's newest 200 runs keep their transcript. An older run answers {success:false,code:"RUN_PROCESS_CLEARED"}; its activity entry still says what it did, and it can no longer be continued.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |
| `runId` | Id of one Digital Human run, the runId in [`GET /api/apps/:appId/activity`](#get-api-apps-appid-activity). |

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{id,role:"user"|"assistant",content,timestamp,thoughts?,thoughtsSummary?,images?}]}
```

**Errors**

- 404 when the app or its space is gone. An empty array means that run left no transcript, not that the ids were wrong.

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/runs/<runId>/session" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Edit part of a digital human's definition (spec) without replacing all of it {#patch-api-apps-appid-spec}

`PATCH /api/apps/:appId/spec` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" />

- A build can refuse remote changes that touch MCP apps (403).

| Name | Description |

| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Request body**

**Response**

```ts
{success:true} | {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX PATCH "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/spec" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"description":"Checks the product page every weekday at 9:00"}'
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/state" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Manually trigger a digital human to run immediately {#post-api-apps-appid-trigger}

`POST /api/apps/:appId/trigger`

- Runs the Digital Human now and answers only after the run has finished, which can take minutes. Use a long client timeout, or follow the run with [`GET /api/apps/:appId/state`](#get-api-apps-appid-state) and the WebSocket instead of waiting on this call.
- If a run is already in progress or queued, the call fails with that message.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId,runId,sessionKey,outcome:"useful"|"noop"|"error"|"skipped",startedAt,finishedAt,durationMs,tokensUsed?,errorMessage?,finalText?}} | {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/trigger" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Set how a store-installed digital human handles version upgrades {#post-api-apps-appid-upgrade-strategy}

`POST /api/apps/:appId/upgrade-strategy` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- strategy is one of "auto" (silent patch/minor, notify on major), "notify" (always notify), or "manual" (no automatic checks)

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `appId` | Digital Human id, from [`GET /api/apps`](#get-api-apps). |

**Request body**

```json
{
  "strategy": "auto"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/<appId>/upgrade-strategy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"strategy":"auto"}'
```

## Install a digital human (or other app type) from a YAML definition (spec) string {#post-api-apps-import-spec}

`POST /api/apps/import-spec`

- Installs a Digital Human (or another app type) from the text of a `spec.yaml`, validated the same way as in the app. Optional `userConfig` fills its configuration fields.
- Unlike installing in the Halo app or through its assistant, this call does not install the skills the spec requires and does not undo a half-finished install.
- A build can refuse remote installs of MCP apps (403).

**Request body**

```json
{
  "spaceId": "<spaceId>",
  "yamlContent": "<contents of spec.yaml>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId}} | {success:false,error,code}
```

**Errors**

- 400 when `spaceId` or `yamlContent` is missing or invalid; other failures carry a `code`.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/import-spec" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spaceId":"<spaceId>","yamlContent":"<contents of spec.yaml>"}'
```

## Install a digital human (or other app type) from its full definition (spec) object {#post-api-apps-install}

`POST /api/apps/install`

- Installs a Digital Human (or a skill or MCP app) from a full spec object, the parsed form of a `spec.yaml`. `spaceId: null` installs a skill or MCP app for every workspace. `userConfig` is optional.
- Unlike installing in the Halo app or through its assistant, this call does not install the skills the spec requires and does not undo a half-finished install. Check [`GET /api/apps/:appId`](#get-api-apps-appid) afterwards.

**Request body**

```ts
{"spaceId": "<spaceId> | null", "spec": {…the parsed spec.yaml…}, "userConfig": {…}}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{appId}} | {success:false,error,code?}
```

**Errors**

- 400 missing `spec` or a `spaceId` that is neither a string nor null, 403 `MCP_COMMAND_BLOCKED` (an MCP command this build's policy blocks), 409 `ALREADY_INSTALLED`, 503 `NOT_INITIALIZED`.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/apps/install" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spaceId":"<spaceId>","spec":{"name":"Price watcher","version":"1.0.0","author":"example","description":"Checks a product page every morning","type":"automation","system_prompt":"Check the product page and report price changes."}}'
```
